plannedCharts.title: Five official numbers for the same ocean
plannedCharts.subtitle: NOAA Nino 3.4 measures for 2026, by product, period and baseline
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Open on the measurement problem rather than a scare number: one ocean, five official NOAA figures, spanning roughly +0.5 to +2.2.

plannedCharts.title: Change the index and the record holder changes
plannedCharts.subtitle: The eight strongest El Nino events since 1950, each measured on the raw index and on the trend-adjusted one - peak seasonal anomaly
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The payoff of the measuring-stick argument: which event counts as the benchmark depends on which index you use.

plannedCharts.title: The measuring stick moved
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average gap between the raw index and the trend-adjusted one (ONI minus RONI), by decade
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The deepest reason old and new El Ninos are hard to compare: as the whole tropical ocean warms, the raw index drifts upward for the same relative Pacific gradient.

plannedCharts.title: A century and a quarter of monsoons that never sit still
plannedCharts.subtitle: IMD all-India June-September rainfall departure - 1901-2025
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Before conditioning on anything, show the raw material: 125 monsoons, no two alike.

plannedCharts.title: How strictly you define an El Nino year changes the answer
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average all-India rainfall departure under three definitions - 1950-2025
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The reassuring headline number and the alarming one come from the same record. The difference is the definition, which most coverage hides.

plannedCharts.title: A bigger El Nino is not a worse monsoon
plannedCharts.subtitle: The seven monsoons in which the ONI reached +1.5 or above during June-September - peak Pacific warmth against India's rainfall departure
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: This is the reference class 2026 belongs to if the forecast holds, and it kills the intuition that a bigger Pacific anomaly means a worse monsoon.

plannedCharts.title: Where the Pacific warmed does not settle it either
plannedCharts.subtitle: Eastern minus central Pacific warmth (Nino 1+2 minus Nino 4, June-September mean) against India's rainfall departure - the seven strong events
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The leading scientific explanation for why some big El Ninos spare India is WHERE the Pacific warms. Tested on these seven events it does not discriminate, which is worth showing rather than hiding.

plannedCharts.title: Does the Indian Ocean rescue an El Nino monsoon?
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average rainfall in El Nino years, split by the Indian Ocean Dipole - 1950-2025
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The second ocean is the most cited reason an El Nino monsoon can come out fine. It works, but only as a tilt.

plannedCharts.title: Has the Pacific's grip on the monsoon loosened?
plannedCharts.subtitle: 21-year rolling correlation between Pacific warmth and India's monsoon rainfall - centred years 1960-2015
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Scientists have argued since the late 1990s that the link is fraying. Track it rather than assert it either way.

plannedCharts.title: El Nino hits the northwest hardest
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average rainfall departure in El Nino monsoons, by IMD region
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The national average hides the geography that decides crops and incomes.

plannedCharts.title: When in the season the rain goes missing
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average monthly rainfall departure, El Nino monsoons against a typical year - all-India
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Timing decides damage: a dry July at sowing hurts far more than a dry September after the crop is set.

plannedCharts.title: Where El Nino actually cuts the rice harvest
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average kharif rice yield change in El Nino monsoons, by state - ICRISAT district data - 1966-2017
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The rainfall map and the harvest map are not the same picture.

plannedCharts.title: Why the rainfall map is not the yield map
plannedCharts.unit: % above or below the recent 5-year normal
plannedCharts.subtitle: El Nino-year yield against the crop's own prior 5-year average: irrigated rice vs rainfed coarse cereals, by region - ICRISAT - 1966-2017
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The northwest loses the most rain yet its rice barely flinches. Splitting an irrigated crop from a rainfed one shows why.

plannedCharts.title: Which crops El Nino actually hits
plannedCharts.unit: % above or below the crop's recent 5-year normal
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average El Nino-year yield against the crop's own prior 5-year normal, all-India - ICRISAT - 1966-2017
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: If irrigation is the shield, the damage should sort cleanly by crop. It does - and the 2026 sowing figures are sorting the same way in real time.

plannedCharts.title: A weak monsoon does not automatically mean dearer food
plannedCharts.subtitle: Post-monsoon (Oct-Dec) wholesale food inflation in El Nino years - RBI WPI - 1982-2024
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The fear behind the headlines is prices. The longest record we have shows the link is real but loose.

plannedCharts.title: After a drought, food prices do not move as one
plannedCharts.subtitle: Post-monsoon wholesale inflation by food group, four El Nino droughts - RBI WPI
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Food inflation is a bundle of separate shocks. Splitting it shows which foods carry the pain.

plannedCharts.title: Same El Nino, opposite signs: India has two monsoons
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average rainfall departure in El Nino conditions - southwest monsoon (all India) against northeast monsoon (southern belt)
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The single most under-covered fact about El Nino in India: it moves rain as well as removing it, and the 2026 event peaks in the season where the sign reverses.

plannedCharts.title: El Nino peaks after the kharif harvest is decided
plannedCharts.subtitle: Every El Nino event since 1950, grouped by the three-month window in which the Pacific reached its maximum
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The fact that moves the risk into 2027: the event is loudest long after the summer crop is settled.

plannedCharts.title: A shrinking share of the economy, but still two in five jobs
plannedCharts.subtitle: Agriculture's share of India's output and of its workforce - 1951-2025
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The human heart of the question: how many people a bad rain year can reach, set against how little it now moves headline GDP.

selectionRules: Start from the page question, not from the indicator name.
Choose the smallest set of visuals that explains scale, trend, structure, comparison, and caveat.
Prefer mobile-friendly charts: line charts with sparse ticks, horizontal bars, share strips, pyramids only when essential, and no dense tables.
Use one strong pull quote only when the evidence supports it with a number.
Add glossary blocks for technical terms that normal readers may not know.
caveats: Use only figures present in lockedNumbers or sourceSummaries.
If a related theme indicator is present, you may use it for context, but do not pretend it is the main answer.
If source coverage is thin, say so directly.
Do not compare states, districts, or cities unless the evidence packet contains those geographies.
forbiddenClaims: Do not infer causality from a trend unless the evidence explicitly supports it.
Do not cite a source that is not present in sourceSummaries.
